summary:
Fixed #1207: compiler warnings can no longer use up a node's line cap and hide the ERROR line that failed it. The fix was already in the worktree when I started (problems.go and problems_test.go were modified). I checked that it meets the issue's expected behaviour and wrote the PR file.

The change is in `problemFilter.admit` in `cli/internal/commands/controlbus/problems.go`. WARN and ERROR lines now have separate per-node budgets: ERROR keeps the cap of 20 (`maxProblemLinesPerNode`), and WARN gets a smaller cap of 10 (`maxWarnLinesPerNode`). Each level prints its own "more problem lines suppressed" notice when it hits its cap.

The new test, `TestProblemFilter_warningsNeverCrowdOutTheError` in `problems_test.go`, sends 60 WARN lines and then an ERROR line. It checks that the warnings stop after 10 lines plus the notice, and that the ERROR line is still printed.

`./gradlew :cli:goTest :cli:goVet :cli:goFormatCheck` passed. The Go test results were cached from an earlier run, but on the current sources. Running `go test` directly needed approval, so I used the Gradle tasks instead. The PR title and description are in `.yukta-dev/pr.md`.
